basics.name: Runguo Li
basics.summary: M.S. student in Information Management at UIUC, working on ML systems for large-scale models: MoE inference engines and expert streaming, KV-cache compression, distributed training and rollout infrastructure, and GPU compiler and kernel-level correctness. 22 merged pull requests across 14 upstream projects, including PyTorch, vLLM, DeepSpeed, LLVM, SGLang, JAX, FlashAttention, Triton, and Megatron-LM. Applying to Ph.D. programs in ML systems for Fall 2028.

education.institution: Shanghai University of Finance and Economics

publications.name: Interrupt Budgets for Pre-Execution AI Control Monitors
publications.summary: Trajectory-level false interruption budgets expose the cost and limits of per-step-calibrated AI control monitors; a 1% per-step threshold interrupts 14–37% of benign LinuxArena runs.

publications.name: Trust but Verify: Diagnosing Causal Prior-Data Fitted Networks and Testing When to Defer
publications.summary: Diagnoses three released causal PFNs against a generic TabPFN-DR baseline and introduces a retraining-free, region-wise deferral wrapper with a paired doubly robust test.

publications.name: AXR: Reusing Intermediate Results for LLM Agents in PostgreSQL
publications.summary: A PostgreSQL extension that materializes plan-subtree results as LLM agents query and reuses them in later plans; 6.5–51.0% less database time on TPC-H with no wrong result in 776,114 checked executions.

publications.name: What Do Group-Conditional Coverage Metrics Measure? Identification, Inference and Auditing for Conformal Evaluation
publications.summary: Separates expected coverage, calibration-draw realized coverage, and test noise; gives sharp identified sets, noise floors, debiased inference, and finite-sample auditing tools for conformal evaluation.

publications.name: Is That Supernode Special? Selection Rules and Null Models Change What Attribution-Graph Interventions Validate
publications.summary: Matched random replacements and two null models test 2,958 automatic and 14 hand-curated supernode claims, showing that selection rules and null choice change which attribution-graph interventions establish feature specificity.

publications.name: Do Search Agents Know When They Know? Answer-State and Evidence Dynamics in RL-Trained Search Agents
publications.summary: An exact replay protocol over seven QA benchmarks shows RL-trained search agents often hold the right answer and then lose it; releases SufficiencyBench with 97,841 decision states.

publications.name: What FP4 Costs Long Reasoning on Blackwell, Measured Above the Noise
publications.summary: Repeated calibration draws, paired tests, and accuracy-budget curves show that FP4 mainly changes reasoning length and memory rather than producing stable accuracy gains.

publications.name: Predict, Don't Just Pair: Lossless Storage for Families of Fine-Tuned Models
publications.summary: Tessera predicts and entropy-codes delta residuals rather than only selecting bases, storing 25.3% of deduplicated bytes across 130 fine-tunes and four model families.

publications.name: What Survives Distillation? A Pre-registered Study of Training-Free Acceleration for Few-Step and Autoregressive Video Diffusion
publications.summary: A pre-registered study of six distilled video-diffusion students showing that teacher-calibrated acceleration signals mislead and that student-local probes yield 2.5–3.5× end-to-end speedups.

publications.name: What Horizon-Aware Losses Do in Multi-Step Forecasting: The L1 Norm, Not Decorrelation
publications.summary: A controlled decomposition shows that recent horizon-aware forecasting losses gain from the L1 norm rather than from decorrelating forecast horizons.

publications.name: How Much Does Random Rotation Help GPTQ? Sharp Worst-Case Rate Gaps in the High-Rate Regime
publications.summary: Sharp worst-case rate gap between randomly rotated GPTQ and WaterSIC via the Lyapunov-exponent limit of Cholesky pivots; median gap 0.04 bit on 96 Qwen3 and Llama-3.1 Hessians.

publications.name: Certified Sparse Attention via Perturbed Retrieval
publications.summary: Sparse attention with per-head error certificates via perturbed retrieval; no certificate violated on three LLMs at 16K–128K tokens, with 4.6–7.9× lower 90th-percentile error than the best of 15 baseline families at equal keys read.

publications.name: Spend Bytes on Breadth: Precision–Count Trade-offs for Decode-Time KV Compression in Long Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
publications.summary: BreadthKV splits a fixed decode-time KV byte budget between token count and precision, beating eviction alone in 17 of 18 settings.
